items.title: How well can measured cellular state predict cell fate?
items.summary: Compare transcriptomic dynamics, observed clonal outcomes, and time-course couplings. Identify where a prediction needs an independent outcome check.

context.scope: A methods comparison across selected studies; performance does not transfer automatically between biological systems.
context.interpretation: Prediction of a later state is distinct from establishing why a cell takes that fate.

provenance.curation: Atlas literature pilot, 2026-09-07; no expert review

items.title: Which gene-regulatory influences help explain fate transitions?
items.summary: Compare expression-based candidate networks with measured responses to genetic perturbations. Ask which observations could support a regulatory explanation.

context.scope: Candidate regulatory influences in specified systems, not a universal gene network.
context.interpretation: Association, a perturbation response, and a direct regulatory mechanism are different claims.

provenance.curation: Atlas literature pilot, 2026-09-07; no expert review

items.title: Transcriptomic dynamics and fate mapping
items.summary: Consider CellRank 2 and veloVI as complementary tools for constructing and examining inferred cell-state dynamics.

context.interpretation: Proposed grouping of methods; shared use here does not establish validated integration.
context.limitation: Inspect the model assumptions and compare inferred fates with independent outcomes.

provenance.curation: Atlas literature pilot, 2026-09-07; no expert review

items.title: Lineage-anchored fate assessment
items.summary: Use the LARRY study to examine what clonal outcomes add to a state-based fate prediction.

context.interpretation: Proposed comparison lens for this pilot.
context.limitation: The included study has temporal-resolution and assay-setting boundaries.

provenance.curation: Atlas literature pilot, 2026-09-07; no expert review

items.title: Time-course transport
items.summary: Consider Waddington-OT when expression is sampled across time and the question concerns population transitions.

context.interpretation: Proposed alternative view of the fate-prediction question.
context.limitation: Compare inferred couplings with available lineage observations before treating them as ancestry.

provenance.curation: Atlas literature pilot, 2026-09-07; no expert review

items.title: Expression-based regulatory network inference
items.summary: Use expression data to nominate candidate links and the BEELINE benchmark to examine the limits of that nomination strategy.

context.interpretation: A candidate-generation approach for this pilot.
context.limitation: Benchmark results are conditional on the evaluated algorithms and reference networks.

provenance.curation: Atlas literature pilot, 2026-09-07; no expert review

items.title: Perturbation-based regulator assessment
items.summary: Compare nominated regulatory influences with measured expression responses to tested genetic perturbations.

context.interpretation: Proposed assessment of candidates; expression response alone is not a complete fate mechanism.
context.limitation: Separate response evidence from claims about direct physical binding or long-term fate.

provenance.curation: Atlas literature pilot, 2026-09-07; no expert review

context.system: human hematopoiesis, endodermal development and organoid examples

items.title: The CellRank transition model is memoryless
items.summary: Its Markov formulation assumes gradual, memoryless transitions when modeling average cellular behavior.

context.limitation: This assumption concerns modeled average behavior; it does not demonstrate that every cell has memoryless dynamics.

items.summary: In the study’s mouse hematopoiesis experiments, lineage information revealed fate biases not detectable from single-cell RNA measurements alone.

context.limitation: This result does not establish that all future transcriptomic methods will miss these biases.

context.limitation: These restrictions apply to the reported strategy, not to all lineage-tracing methods.

items.title: Compare predictions with held-out clonal outcomes
items.summary: Proposed study question: compare state-based fate predictions with clonal outcomes excluded from model fitting, while matching the system and observation window.

context.interpretation: Study proposal only; no experiment or model comparison has been run.
context.result_that_would_change_interpretation: If clonal outcomes systematically disagree with predicted fate probabilities in the matched setting, narrow the applicability claim and examine missing state information.
context.limitation: Predefine the evaluation split, outcome definitions and temporal resolution before interpreting agreement.

subject: cell fate
system: a matched lineage dataset, to be selected

items.title: Compare candidate links with matched-state perturbation responses
items.summary: Proposed study question: assess whether candidate regulatory links anticipate expression responses to perturbations in matched cellular states.

context.interpretation: Study proposal only; no perturbations have been performed for this pilot.
context.result_that_would_change_interpretation: If candidate links fail to anticipate responses after suitable controls, weaken the regulatory interpretation; agreement would motivate further mechanism and fate-outcome checks.
context.limitation: State matching, controls and direct-versus-indirect effects need a study-specific design.

subject: gene regulation
system: a matched perturbation dataset, to be selected
